summary: Backend test for Geo autocomplete + referral_engine / bot_personalization / admin_viewers endpoints. 16/18 passed, 1 failed (route shadowing), 1 skipped (admin auth). All 6 geo test cases PASS as specified. Detected route-collision between legacy routes/referral.py and new routes/referral_engine.py.

minor.issue: Route collision: both routes/referral.py (registered line 246) and routes/referral_engine.py (registered line 484) define /api/referral/leaderboard with same prefix. FastAPI resolves to first-registered (referral.py), which calls get_current_user(request) and returns 401 despite docstring claiming 'public leaderboard'. The new referral_engine.leaderboard() (documented public) is SHADOWED and never reached. Fix: either change prefix of referral_engine_router (e.g. /api/referral/v2) OR remove duplicate endpoint from referral.py OR drop the auth call on the legacy leaderboard.

Same route-collision: /apply exists in BOTH referral.py and referral_engine.py. First-registered (referral.py) wins, so the new referral_engine.apply() handler is SHADOWED and unreachable. Tests pass on the shadow (both return auth-required), but behaviourally the engine-version is dead code. Recommend deduplicating.

test_results_by_case.POST /api/referral/apply: PASS (403/422) — endpoint exists (but see shadowing issue)
test_results_by_case.GET /api/referral/leaderboard: FAIL — returns 401 (shadowed by legacy referral.py that calls get_current_user)
test_results_by_case.GET /api/admin/audit/list (admin auth): PASS 401 (unauth) — endpoint wired; admin-login skipped (no auth token available via /api/auth/login)

action_items: Resolve route collision on /api/referral/leaderboard and /api/referral/apply between routes/referral.py (legacy) and routes/referral_engine.py (new). Recommended: change referral_engine prefix to /api/referral/v2 OR delete shadowed endpoints from referral.py.
routes/referral.py leaderboard calls get_current_user() despite docstring saying 'public'. Remove auth call if public intent, or update docstring.
critical_code_review_comments: Route-prefix duplication: two different router files both register prefix='/api/referral'. FastAPI silently shadows later-registered duplicates; second handlers become dead code with no warning. Add a startup check or rename prefix.

rca of the issue: GET /api/referral/leaderboard returns 401 because FastAPI router registration order matters: routes/referral.py is registered at server.py L246 with prefix '/api/referral' and defines GET /leaderboard that calls get_current_user(request). The newer routes/referral_engine.py registered at L484 with the same prefix also defines GET /leaderboard (public) but is shadowed and never invoked. Mitigation: rename one of the prefixes (e.g., /api/referral/v2) or deduplicate the legacy handler.
